source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-03: column 15 splits the rows into two halves of 64; the half with 0 there is the CKRS 2010 cross-sum CA(64; 5, 14, 2) (as built by CAs::ckrsCA(5, 14, 2)), and the half with 1 is a CA(64; 5, 14, 2) found by simulated annealing so that the union of the two halves has strength 6 on the first 14 columns; exact check with ca_verify, all 5005 column 6-sets
construction: Two strength-5 halves split by one column (the CKRS cross-sum array and an annealed partner), union of strength 6
notes: equals the Torres-Jimenez size 128 at k = 15; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start; the split by one column is the principle of the tower construction of Torres-Jimenez, Izquierdo-Marquez, Kacker and Kuhn 2015, credited as a method
